terms.grammar: noun, third declension: accusative vim, ablative vī; plural vīrēs, strength
evidence: Cic. Mil. 9: cum vī vīs illāta dēfenditur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: vī or per vim, by force; vim adhibēre, to use force; vim afferre alicui, to do violence to someone (Lewis & Short). The force of wind or water is vīs too. Armed forces are cōpiae.

phrases.latin: Ratiōne, nōn vī vincenda adulēscentia est.
phrases.english: youth is to be won over by reason, not by force

phrases.latin: Nōlī vim adhibēre; operculum suā sponte sequētur.
phrases.english: Don’t force it: the lid will come off by itself.

sources: Lewis & Short: vis · Lewis & Short: copia · Lewis & Short: sequor
